one_line_summary: Upright recreational running posture captured during mid-flight phase.

findings.title: Head & Neck Alignment
findings.observation: Gaze is directed forward with neutral cervical spine alignment.
findings.tldr: Head position is stable and aligned with torso.
findings.eli5: You are looking straight ahead like scanning the horizon. This keeps your posture balanced.
findings.evidence: Neutral head carriage preserves kinetic chain alignment and reduces cervical extensor load.

findings.title: Shoulder Position
findings.observation: Shoulders are slightly elevated with minor tension apparent.
findings.eli5: Your shoulders are slightly shrugged. Dropping them saves energy.
findings.evidence: Excessive shoulder girdle elevation increases unnecessary upper-body metabolic expenditure.

findings.title: Arm Carriage & Drive
findings.observation: Arm swing is sagittal, though elbow flexion opens slightly on the rearward drive.
findings.tldr: Functional arm swing with minor excess forearm extension.
findings.eli5: Your arms pump well, but the elbow opens up a bit too wide in back. Keep elbows bent near a right angle.
findings.evidence: Compact arm levers optimize rotational counterbalancing of torso inertia.

findings.title: Trunk & Posture
findings.observation: Trunk is relatively vertical with minimal whole-body forward lean.
findings.tldr: Torso is upright with limited forward propulsion lean.
findings.eli5: You are standing quite tall while moving forward. Leaning slightly forward helps momentum.
action: Cue a slight forward lean from ankles
findings.evidence: A subtle full-body lean facilitates forward center-of-mass propulsion and gluteal recruitment.

findings.title: Knee Drive & Swing
findings.observation: Moderate swing-phase knee flexion and controlled anterior drive.
findings.tldr: Swing mechanics show adequate forward knee carriage.
findings.eli5: Your knees drive forward adequately for this speed. It produces smooth forward motion.
findings.evidence: Adequate swing-leg flexion shortens pendulum length, optimizing recovery cadence.

insufficient.title: Pelvic Drop & Stability
insufficient.why: Frontal plane pelvic stability cannot be assessed from a profile perspective.

insufficient.title: Foot Strike & Overstride
insufficient.why: Runner is in flight phase without ground contact; impact mechanics cannot be evaluated.
